name: Hirschsprung Disease-Type D Brachydactyly Syndrome
aliases: Hirschsprung Disease with Type D Brachydactyly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Hirschsprung Disease-Type D Brachydactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Histopathological evidence of aganglionosis in the distal colon
Presence of brachydactyly type D characterized by hypoplasia or aplasia of the distal phalanx of the thumbs
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with Hirschsprung disease and brachydactyly type D
Clinical presentation including chronic constipation and abdominal distension in neonates or infants

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of aganglionosis plus presence of brachydactyly type D and/or relevant pathogenic genetic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, clinical examination, and genetic testing.

common.symptomName: Short distal phalanx of the thumb

laboratory: Histopathology showing absence of ganglion cells in submucosal and myenteric plexuses
Routine blood tests may show electrolyte imbalances secondary to obstruction
imaging: Contrast enema demonstrating transition zone in colon
Radiographs showing shortened distal phalanx of thumbs
genetic: Pathogenic variants in RET, EDNRB, or other Hirschsprung-associated genes
Genetic markers associated with brachydactyly type D
other: Anorectal manometry showing absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated gastrointestinal symptoms without skeletal anomalies
Presence of brachydactyly type D without gastrointestinal symptoms
Hirschsprung disease with intellectual disability and facial dysmorphism
Distinct genetic mutation in ZEB2 gene

redFlags: Failure to pass meconium within 48 hours of birth
Signs of enterocolitis such as fever, diarrhea, and sepsis
references: Orphanet: Hirschsprung disease-type D brachydactyly syndrome (ORPHA:2150)
Amiel J, et al. Hirschsprung disease, associated syndromes and genetics: a review. J Med Genet. 2008.
Fukuzawa R, et al. Brachydactyly type D: clinical and radiographic features. J Hand Surg Am. 2001.
